hero.title: MirDB
hero.tagline: Persistent key-value store with the Memcached protocol — built in Rust.

features.title: Memcached Protocol
features.description: Drop-in compatibility with existing Memcached clients.

features.title: Built in Rust
features.description: Memory-safe systems language with zero-cost abstractions.

features.title: Persistent Storage
features.description: Durable on-disk storage instead of pure in-memory.

features.title: Skip-list Memtable
features.description: Concurrent in-memory data structure with logarithmic lookups.

features.title: Write-Ahead Log
features.description: Durability and crash recovery via WAL.

features.title: Compaction
features.description: Background compaction keeps storage compact and reads fast.

codeExample.description: Connect with any Memcached client. Here are the basics over the text protocol:
codeExample.snippet:
# Start the server
mirdb-server --port 11211

# In another shell, use any memcached client:
set hello 0 0 5
world
# STORED

get hello
# VALUE hello 0 5
# world
# END

add counter 0 0 1
0
# STORED

replace hello 0 0 5
MirDB
# STORED

delete counter
# DELETED

whyMirDB.difference: MirDB persists data to disk — values survive restarts.
MirDB keeps the surface tiny by speaking the Memcached protocol.
MirDB ships a network protocol out of the box; RocksDB is embedded only.
